title: A thin foreground dust screen has an absorbed-power floor when forward scattering fills its dips
abstract: We derive a lower bound on absorbed power for a thin foreground dust screen around a finite uniform star. The bound allows every projected cloud shape and local albedo. A sorted area construction attains it in a first-order transfer model. An independent linear program checks the result. For a representative CPV test at 1.95 stellar radii, a 4.74% dip and extinction optical depth at most 0.1, the lowest relative absorbed power is 0.489 for a Henyey-Greenstein phase function with mean cosine 0.9, and 0.902 at 0.98. These exceed an imposed fixed-spectrum limit of 0.290 taken from a published population infrared fit. The comparison is conditional: that limit is not an individual-star limit, the thermal spectrum is held fixed, and no physical grain composition is fitted. We also prove sharp bounds on stellar-cone scattering given only its mean cosine. They show that a mean cosine alone cannot determine dip filling. Opaque cores, phase-dependent reference light, non-grey emission and multiple scattering remain outside the main test. Code, proofs, aggregate source provenance, two numerical grids and figures are included. No new dust detection or direct observational exclusion is claimed.

display.caption: The lowest absorbed-power ratio for arbitrary cloud shape and local albedo in a first-order HG foreground screen. The infrared line defines a representative fixed-template test, not an individual-star confidence limit. Caps of 0.3 and 1 are formal first-order sensitivity tests; transfer at unity optical depth is not controlled.
